pageCache.text:
SEND and Inclusion
Special Educational Needs & Disability (SEND)
As an ODST school, the leaders and governors endeavour to make every effort to achieve maximum inclusion of all pupils whilst meeting pupils’ individual needs. As a school we recognise the entitlement of all pupils to a broad and balanced curriculum. The SEND policy and school vision reinforces the need for teaching that is fully inclusive. The Local Governing Body will ensure that appropriate provision will be made for all pupils with SEND.
The four main areas of special educational need are broadly defined as:
As a school we aim to:
Cognition and Learning
Communication and Interaction
Social, Emotional and Mental Health
Sensory and physical needs
To be an inclusive school
SENCo
Our school Special Educational Needs Coordinator (SENCo) is Holly Docherty. She has dedicated time each week to support both children and families and can be contacted via the school office 01993 822159.

Clubs
We offer a wide range of extra-curricular clubs at Burford Primary School. These will always include a sports club and teacher led clubs each half term. This has included:
Our club provision is regularly reviewed through our school council meeting. If your child has a particular interest in the club, or you have a passion which you would be willing to share with our children, please do contact the school office.
Arts and craft club – encouraging creativity
Chess club – developing children’s strategic thinking
Eco Council
Our School Council
The School Council got together over a number of occasions to work on a new set of school rules that are easy to remember both in the classroom and at play. They decided that rules that begin with "Be ..." are better than "Don't ..." and "Always ..." Once they'd decided this, they looked through a large number of possible "Be..." rules before coming to a unanimous decision that they wanted 3 rules only and they needed to be in this order: "Be Safe", "Be Ready" and "Be Respectful".
Then they worked out on their poster design to display in every classroom and in shared areas around school.
In preparation for launching the new school rules to the whole school community, the children practised their actions.
